questions.stem: Sea area A1 is within the coverage of:
options: a VHF coast station with continuous DSC alerting
an MF coast station with continuous DSC alerting
a satellite service such as Inmarsat
no coast station, so ships call each other
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 200 defines A1 by VHF coverage with continuous DSC alerting.

questions.stem: Which sea area is outside A1 but within MF coast station coverage?
options: A1
A3
A4
A2
questions.explanation: A2 is outside A1 and within MF coverage; A3 is satellite coverage; A4 is everything else.

questions.stem: About how far does the RAMN say A1 and A2 extend?
options: About 5 nm for A1 and 20 nm for A2
About 100 nm for A1 and 400 nm for A2
About 40 nm for A1 and 150 nm for A2
About 40 nm for both A1 and A2
questions.explanation: RAMN gives roughly 40 nautical miles for A1 and 150 for A2.

options: It is the same as the vessel's radio call sign
A nine-digit identifier programmed into the DSC radio
It is a five-digit number issued with the station licence
It is only needed on international voyages
questions.explanation: RAMN: VHF/DSC equipment must be programmed with the correct nine-digit MMSI.

questions.stem: Which VHF channel is used for DSC?
options: Channel 70 (156.525 MHz)
Channel 16 (156.800 MHz)
Channel 13 (156.650 MHz)
Channel 21B (161.650 MHz)
questions.explanation: DSC alert traffic is on Channel 70.

options: Distress, weather, tides, ship's business and routine
Mayday, pan-pan and securite only, with no routine calls
Emergency, navigational, commercial and personal
Distress, urgency, safety, ship's business and routine
questions.explanation: RIC-25 syllabus lists these call categories.

questions.stem: How is a DSC distress alert started on VHF, and what follows?
options: Tap the button once; the radio does the rest
Hold it down for 30 seconds; voice follows on Channel 70
Hold the red button 5 seconds; voice follows on Channel 16
Press it twice; voice follows on Channel 13
questions.explanation: RAMN: press and hold the red distress button for 5 seconds, then send the distress call and message on Channel 16.

questions.stem: A ship hears a DSC distress alert on VHF. Which statement is correct?
options: It must relay at once by DSC
It must not send a DSC relay
It must acknowledge by DSC at once
It must switch off DSC
questions.explanation: RAMN: a ship may not send a DSC distress relay after receiving a DSC distress alert on VHF or MF.

questions.stem: A ship receives an all-stations DSC safety announcement. It:
options: must not acknowledge receipt
must acknowledge at once
must relay it
must switch to Channel 70 voice
questions.explanation: RAMN: a ship receiving an all-stations DSC safety announcement shall not acknowledge it.

options: Port fees, berth lists and pilot times
Tide tables and current predictions only
Crew lists sent to the traffic centre
Navigational and weather warnings and urgent safety messages
questions.explanation: That is the NSR 2020 s. 200 definition.

questions.stem: On what frequency does the international NAVTEX service broadcast in English?
options: 518 kHz
2182 kHz
questions.explanation: NSR 2020 s. 200: international NAVTEX is on 518 kHz.

questions.stem: Which vessels must be able to reach an MCTS centre at any time on a voyage with part outside A1 (s. 206)?
options: Any vessel over 5 m in length
A vessel that carries more than six passengers
Only vessels over 500 GT
Only fishing vessels over 15 GT
questions.explanation: Section 206 covers vessels carrying passengers more than 2 nm from shore, more than six passengers, or on a Near Coastal Class 1 or unlimited voyage.

questions.stem: DSC is defined in NSR 2020 as a system of digital codes that conforms to:
options: ITU-R Recommendation M.493
IMO resolution A.814(19)
SOLAS Chapter II, regulation 2
IEC 60945 only, for all equipment
questions.explanation: Section 200 defines DSC by reference to ITU-R M.493. A.814(19) is the false alert guideline.

questions.stem: Which two NAVTEX transmitters does Prince Rupert MCTS use on the BC coast?
options: Mount Parke and Bowen Island
Race Rocks and Sandheads
Cape Lazo and Texada Island light stations
Digby Island and Amphitrite Point
questions.explanation: RAMN Parts 2 and 5 list Digby Island and Amphitrite Point as NAVTEX transmitters.
